items.q: Match the onset and oedema of the two syndromes — 1) Nephrotic syndrome  2) Nephritic syndrome … A) Abrupt onset with intravascular (++) oedema  B) Insidious onset with extravascular (+++) oedema
items.exp: Onset/oedema: nephrotic = insidious with extravascular (+++) oedema; nephritic = abrupt with intravascular (++) oedema. (Book p777)

items.q: Match the BP and JVP of the two syndromes — 1) Nephrotic syndrome  2) Nephritic syndrome … A) BP high, JVP raised  B) BP normal, JVP normal
items.exp: Nephrotic syndrome: BP normal, JVP normal. Nephritic syndrome: BP high, JVP raised. (Book p777)

items.q: Match the urine findings of the two syndromes — 1) Nephrotic syndrome  2) Nephritic syndrome … A) Proteinuria more, haematuria less, RBC casts absent  B) Proteinuria less, haematuria more, RBC casts present
items.exp: Nephrotic: proteinuria more, haematuria less, RBC casts absent. Nephritic: proteinuria less, haematuria more, RBC casts present. (Book p777)

items.q: A 4-year-old has generalised pitting oedema, BP 95/60 mmHg, normal JVP and 4+ proteinuria with no RBC casts. Serum albumin is low. Which syndrome does this describe?
items.exp: Nephrotic syndrome: insidious onset, extravascular (+++) oedema, normal BP and JVP, more proteinuria, less haematuria, absent RBC casts and low serum albumin. (Book p777)

items.q: A 7-year-old presents with cola-coloured urine, BP 140/95 mmHg and raised JVP, with 1+ albuminuria and RBC casts; serum albumin is 3.9 g/dL. Which syndrome is this?
items.exp: Nephritic syndrome: abrupt onset, high BP, raised JVP (intravascular ++ oedema), less proteinuria, more haematuria, RBC casts present and normal or slightly low serum albumin. (Book p777)

items.q: Which serum albumin finding belongs to nephrotic syndrome and NOT to nephritic syndrome?
items.exp: Serum albumin is low in nephrotic syndrome, whereas in nephritic syndrome it is normal or only slightly decreased. (Book p777)

items.q: Fill up: In the nephrotic vs nephritic table, the oedema of nephrotic syndrome is mainly ______.
items.exp: Oedema: nephrotic = extravascular (+++); nephritic = intravascular (++). (Book p777)

items.q: RBC casts are a feature of the nephritic syndrome and are absent in nephrotic syndrome.
opts: False — RBC casts are present in both
False — RBC casts are found only in nephrotic syndrome
True, but only after 8 weeks of illness
items.exp: The table lists RBC casts as absent (–) in nephrotic syndrome and present (+) in nephritic syndrome. (Book p777)

items.q: Comparing proteinuria and haematuria, the nephritic syndrome is characterised by:
items.exp: Nephritic: proteinuria less, haematuria more. Nephrotic: proteinuria more, haematuria less. (Book p777)
